claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic high-entropy alloy has an as-cast lamellar microstructure.
Adding approximately 0.5 wt.% boron during controlled casting will produce nanoscale boride particles.
Real-time process monitoring can ensure or optimize nanoscale boride nucleation and growth.
Controlled cooling under an inert atmosphere will ensure uniform boron distribution and in situ formation of nanometer-scale borides.
The boride dispersoids will be uniformly distributed at the lamellar interfaces.
Boron will react with matrix elements to form stable boride particles.
Finely dispersed boride particles will impede dislocation motion through dispersion strengthening.
Impedance of dislocation motion by the boride particles will increase yield strength.
Keeping the boride particles nanoscale will allow the ductile matrix to accommodate plastic strain.
A uniform nanoscale boride distribution will preserve or improve ductility relative to the boron-free alloy.
The boron-modified alloy will have higher yield strength than the boron-free baseline.
The proposed strength and ductility improvements depend on keeping the boron content near 0.5 wt.%, controlling the cooling rate, and retaining nanoscale borides.
Departures from the specified boron content or cooling conditions may produce coarse particles.
Coarse boride particles may embrittle the alloy.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that both strength and ductility will be enhanced, whereas the predicted outcome and falsification rule only require ductility to be maintained. Thus, the required ductility outcome alternates between a strict increase and non-degradation.
